Messages.Author: Neil Bernstein
Messages.Body:
Saturday night. Playing Malkavians. Hand jam. Damn! Wait... maybe I
can get rid of one card. Concealed Weapon. But no weapon in my hand. Damn!

Well, I played it anyway: as combat began, I said "Ozmo attempts to equip
a weapon with Concealed Weapon... but I have no weapon in my hand so the
card has no effect." Was this allowable? Or is it the same crime as adding
stealth when you're not blocked (or adding intercept when there's no
stealth on the action you're blocking)?

Same time, same place, same hand jam. During master phase I played
Misdirection, and set x to 0. Allowable? Or not, under the same theory?

Thanks for your help,

- Neil

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
You can certainly play an X card with an X of 0, so can play Misdirection
for 0 just to get rid of it. This uses up a master phase action, of course.

You can also add blood to a vampire, or refill a vampire, that is already
at capacity. So you can waste Giant's Blood on a full vampire if you want.

Playing Disguised (or Concealed) Weapon with no weapons in hand is a bit
murkier, though. It's unclear whether this is one of those "success is not
required" actions, like playing a useless strike, or one of those "you must
be doing something useful" actions, like trying to increase stealth.
I'll have to find out which way we want to go with this.

Messages.Author: Stuart J. Pieloch
Messages.Body:
nwbe...@unix.amherst.edu (Neil Bernstein) writes:
>Well, I played it anyway: as combat began, I said "Ozmo attempts to equip
>a weapon with Concealed Weapon... but I have no weapon in my hand so the
>card has no effect." Was this allowable? Or is it the same crime as adding
>stealth when you're not blocked (or adding intercept when there's no
>stealth on the action you're blocking)?

>Same time, same place, same hand jam. During master phase I played
>Misdirection, and set x to 0. Allowable? Or not, under the same theory?

As far as I can tell from WotC
Jyhad and V:TES rules allow you to play a combat card to no effect.
They also allow you to play a master with X in it's cost as 0.
Useful for removing a hand jam,
but not terribly powerful
Similarly, playing a threats modifier to a bleed is legal in
response to a block. It may not make any sense logically
that you would want to increase the bleed associated with a blocked action
but then Superior Form of Mist may make it worthwhile.

So yes, play them as you did. This is a rule that may be House Rule
Overridden though, so officaly feel free to play this way unless everyone
else hinks it's wrong.

Messages.Author: Jeff Dai
Messages.Body:
Here's a bit of a twist to the question.

I've done this several times to the horror of my prey. A Malkavian with
superior obfuscate gets intercepted when attempting a massive bleed (I
know not possible but my prey had a gangrel with three raven spies, cat's
guidence, KRCG, and a sport's bike and me with only two stealth cards in
the hand). Anyways we get into combat. I have no weapon in hand but
know that my deck is full of guns. I play the disguised weapon and pick
up the next card. Presto a saturday night special which I proceed to use
to jump to long range and Dragon's breath rounds come out of the
disguised gun and "POOF" there goes the blocker.

To say the least my opponent was not pleased

Just an amusing note of fun

Jeff
